articles.title: President Trump awards Big Tech donors with nation’s highest science prizes
articles.full_text:
On Thursday, at the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit, President Trump awarded Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and AMD’s Lisa Su the National Medal of Science, the nation’s top science prize. Dell Technologies’ Michael Dell and Microsoft’s Satya Nadella also received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

Together, the awardees have donated nearly $6 billion to efforts tied to Trump and his administration, according to The New Republic. Alphabet and Microsoft, for example, donated to the president’s inauguration fund and White House ballroom. AMD gave to a pro-Trump Super PAC, and Michael and Susan Dell pledged $6.25 billion to help fund the Trump Accounts, the administration’s savings program for children. 

Trump said the honorees had helped “pioneer an incredible future for America,” and that because of them, “we will always be on top. No one else can compete with us.” 

Nadella received his medal right after the administration indefinitely suspended Microsoft from the H-1B program, which lets U.S. companies hire skilled foreign workers.
articles.summary:
President Trump awarded the National Medal of Science and National Medal of Technology and Innovation to several top tech leaders during the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit on Thursday, drawing attention to the substantial financial ties between the honorees and his administration.

  • Core Event: Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and AMD's Lisa Su received the National Medal of Science, while Michael Dell and Microsoft's Satya Nadella were given the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Trump praised the group for helping "pioneer an incredible future for America."
  • Background: According to The New Republic, the awardees have collectively donated nearly $6 billion to efforts tied to Trump and his administration, including inauguration funds, a White House ballroom project, a pro-Trump Super PAC, and the Trump Accounts children's savings program.
  • Notable Timing: Nadella received his medal shortly after the administration indefinitely suspended Microsoft from the H-1B program, which allows U.S. companies to hire skilled foreign workers — an awkward juxtaposition given Microsoft's reliance on such visas.
  • Impact: The ceremony highlights the increasingly intertwined relationship between the tech industry's most powerful figures and the Trump administration, raising questions about the role of political donations in national honors and policy treatment.
